findings.title: Every success criterion traces to a task
findings.description:
Cross-reference against the slice design's 11 Functional SCs and 7 Technical SCs:

- Functional F1 (slice-branch body cites design, tasks, review) → Tasks 7, 8, 9, 11, 13
- F2 (unplanned repo: five sections, three no-input lines, creation succeeds) → Tasks 5, 11, 13
- F3 (merged-ancestor review excluded) → Task 8.2's load-bearing test
- F4 (refusal when configured branch absent from host) → Task 5.1's third row + Task 5.2's refusal-case test
- F5 (present integration branch used, source printed) → Task 5.1, Task 13.1
- F6 (missing push and behind-push failures) → Task 6
- F7 (presence-check failure creates nothing) → Tasks 12, 13
- F8 (title: human name when slice, fallback to first commit subject) → Task 10a
- F9 (dry-run equals real) → Task 13.1's "bound once" rule, Task 13.2's equality test
- F10 (operator-unidentified refuses, no write) → Tasks 13.1 ordering, 14 parametrized over identify_operator
- F11 (one recorded live creation) → Task 16.2 step 5
- Technical T1 (timeouts per call site) → Task 14.1
- T2 (provider failure logged, no write) → Task 10.1 boundary handler, Task 10.2 test
- T3 (default path makes exactly one write after reads) → Task 13.1 ordering, Task 13.2
- T4 (review/ does not import pr/) → Task 15.1
- T5 (checkbox parser real-file fixture) → Task 2.2
- T6 (pyright/ruff clean) → Task 16.1
- T7 (summary_oneshot docstring + test) → Task 15.2

Verification Walkthrough steps 1–6 → Task 16.2; walkthrough rewrite with observed output → Task 16.3.

findings.title: Sequencing follows the design's implementation order with no cycles
findings.description: The task order matches the LLD's "Implementation Notes → Order": parsers (1, 2) → git helpers (3) → `resolve_locator` extraction (4) → refusal paths (5, 6) → inputs (7, 8) → assembly (9) → body layers (10, 10a, 11, 12) → command wiring (13) → failure matrix (14) → corrections (15) → verification (16). Dependencies between tasks are forward-only and explicit where they exist (e.g., Task 1 needed by Task 7, Task 4 needed by Task 13, Task 2 needed by Task 7, Task 3 needed by Task 7). The failure-matrix task (14) sits after the command (13) it tests. No cycles.

findings.title: Test-with pattern is respected; no test calls a real model
findings.description: Each implementation task (1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, 7.1, 8.1, 9.1, 10.1, 10a.1, 11.1, 12.1, 13.1) has an immediately-following test task with concrete cases tied back to the design's decision. Task 10.2 explicitly states "No test here calls a real model" and the context summary confirms the model is exercised live exactly once, in Task 16.2.

findings.title: Proportionality holds; no overweight sub-tasks
findings.description: The slice is substantial (8 design decisions, 18 SCs, 6 verification steps, a new 7-file package plus three file modifications). 16 tasks is proportionate. Sub-tasks are small (most Effort 1 or 2; the largest are 8.1, 8.2, 11.1, 13.1, 13.2, 14.1 at Effort 3, each with a tight focus). The single task file is appropriate — splitting would not improve clarity.

findings.title: No NFR-restated load test owed; no implicit CI gating
findings.description: The slice design does not restate a quantifiable throughput, latency, or capacity NFR. The "live creation" requirement is a one-shot verification, exercised once in Task 16.2 step 5 — not a load-test scenario. No `tests/load/` task is needed and no CI wiring is left implicit.

findings.title: No `**Commit**:` markers in the file
findings.description: The file contains no commit markers. Per the review criteria, "A file with no markers is acceptable; do not require them." Recording this as an observation, not a finding — the breakdown is otherwise complete.
